title: Crossing the Validation Crisis: Cross-Validation Reduces Benchmarking Variance Surprisingly Well
mechanism: Repeated cross-validation splits act as a virtual enlargement of the test set (sample gain); gains keep growing past K=5 and an early-stop rule from split redundancy says when to stop.
adaptation: Module-grouped repeated CV over the 532 train+val cells using the existing fold roots (2 groupings x 5 folds), paired per split and seed; pooled out-of-fold crack/inactive IoU as the decision instrument; test-49 and E1 kept untouched for confirmation. Also lets logit bias / checkpoint be chosen on 532 OOF cells instead of 54 val cells.
min_experiment: Arm: house and PF on 10 grouped splits, 1 seed each, paired. Baseline: 5v5 seeds on clean test-49. Metric: SE of paired delta in pooled OOF crack IoU and minimum detectable effect (2.8 x SE). Kill: CV MDE not <= 0.008 (vs ~0.012 now).
evidence: R: MCCV at K=200 gave test-sample gain ~14 (Ridge) and ~15 (MLP) on synthetic data; real data (PCam histopathology CNNs/ViT, Yelp BERT) gains of about 5 to 20 at K=20, not converged at K=5; repeated K-fold comparable.
prior_overlap: BRIEF 4.5 notes grouped 5-fold roots exist; section 5 'never tried' lists k-fold cross-validated selection. Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Make module-grouped 5-fold CV over 532 cells the primary comparison, clean-49 test and E1 as held-out reports; OOF predictions double as label-audit input.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Compare seed-pair standard error of crack IoU difference on CV vs clean-49 for house vs PF. Kill: none (measurement design).
